transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-08-19
Start time: 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Raman (Redwood SE), Samir Gupta (Redwood Security PM), Maya Patel (SentinelHealth Head of Security), Carlos Ruiz (Platform Eng), Dr. Alan Cho (CTO), Rina Gomez (Privacy Officer)
---
[00:00] Jordan: ok everyone thanks for joining, this is the weekly security sync for the pilot with SentinelHealth. quick roll call?
[00:08] Maya: hey Maya here, Maya Pat- uh Patel, Head of Sec, quick hello.
[00:11] Carlos: Carlos here, platform, will be running the tests.
[00:14] Dr. Cho: Alan Cho, CTO, on for a bit.
[00:18] Rina: Rina Gomez, privacy.
[00:20] Jordan: great, from Redwood we've got Priya and Samir as well. objective today: SSO progress, audit logs retention/export, data retention questions during the pilot, and SOC 2 artifacts.
[00:35] Priya: quick status from our side on SSO - we pushed the SAML metadata to your staging tenant yesterday, you should have the metadata URL in the deck link I sent. we saw an issue with the nameID format on one test assertion, that seems to be a attributes mapping mismatch.
[00:50] Carlos: yeah, we saw a 400 on the assertion, it said invalid name id, we were using email as the NameID but your doc seemed to expect persistent id, so we want to confirm which attributes you require.
[01:05] Priya: right, our default is email but for enterprise we recommend persistent NameID to avoid account duplication. we can support both, you need to include email, given_name, last_name, and an employee id if possible.
[01:20] Maya: ok we'll validate, but legal wants to confirm we don't send PHI in assertions. can you confirm what user attributes are logged?
[01:29] Samir: good question. SAML assertions are not stored in full in production logs, we only record identifiers for auth events. I will double-check exact fields in the audit logs, but policy is we avoid logging raw PHI. there may be snippets in trace contexts but we mask sensitive fields.
[01:45] Rina: we need the explicit list though, we have to sign off from privacy.
[01:49] Samir: noted, action for me to produce the audit log schema and redaction rules.
[01:55] Jordan: next topic, audit log retention. currently in the staging tenant we have 30 days by default, and hosted has 30 days unless you buy extended retention. for the pilot you requested 90 days, correct?
[02:08] Maya: yes, we want 90 days in staging and an export capability to ship logs to our SIEM (we use Splunk).
[02:15] Priya: we can enable 90 days in staging, and we have a syslog/S3 export feature. we can provide a sample CloudWatch-to-S3 or syslog pipeline.
[02:28] Carlos: will the logs contain raw prompts or model outputs? that's our big concern for PHI.
[02:35] Samir: important nuance: we have tiered logging. full request/response body logging is off by default for hosted; for audit we log metadata about calls, tokens consumed, model name, redwood request id, and user id. request/response content is stored only if you opt-in for debug traces. for the pilot we recommend keeping debug traces disabled.
[02:55] Maya: can you show how to export without the payload? our compliance team wants logs without the request body.
[03:02] Priya: yes, export can be configured to exclude payloads; the export schema includes flags to omit content. i'll attach an export config example.
[03:10] Jordan: quick note - there was a small inconsistency in the docs where KV cache was written as KV cash in one place, ignore that it's a typo.
[03:18] Carlos: (laughs) yeah saw that.
[03:22] Maya: SOC 2 - we need to review your latest report and the mapping to our control framework. also will need any subservice org descriptions.
[03:31] Jordan: we can share the SOC 2 Type II report and the security whitepaper. samir will attach the audit mapping matrix.
[03:37] Samir: yes I'll include the SOC 2 PDF, our continuous monitoring evidence, and a brief mapping to common healthcare controls. one caveat: the SOC 2 report may have redactions for customer names, if you need the full unredacted we can discuss an NDA.
[03:53] Rina: we'll likely need the unredacted for our auditors, ok let's follow up on NDA if required.
[03:58] Carlos: a technical question about private deployment - for later stages we may look at private (VPC) deployment. how different is the audit log path in that setup?
[04:08] Priya: in Private deployments the control plane is customer managed or we can run the private control plane; logs stay in your VPC and never hit Redwood's shared logging infrastructure. exports are direct to your S3 or Splunk HEC.
[04:19] Dr. Cho: and what about KMS/HSM integrations? we need BYOK options.
[04:24] Samir: we support customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM integration for Private. for Dedicated we support KMS in the cloud provider; for on-prem we can integrate with HSM via PKCS#11.
[04:36] Maya: great. question on data retention for embeddings - we plan to index embeddings for retrieval within our application. will those be persisted and are they considered customer data we can purge?
[04:47] Priya: embeddings stored in your tenant are customer data and you can purge them via API or retention policies. we tag vectors with ttl and retention. by default vectors are retained until deletion; we'll show the purge API.
[04:58] Carlos: can we automate purge after 30 days unless flagged?
[05:02] Priya: yes you can set TTL on ingestion or run batch deletes. we'll provide the script.
[05:08] Maya: another ask: for the pilot, we'd like a short-term agreement that logs with PHI are excluded from exports and that debug traces are disabled unless explicit opt-in. can you confirm?
[05:20] Jordan: yes we can formalize that in the pilot config; add to next steps.
[05:25] Samir: also note that our model-hosting runtime has a KV cache for speed; we ensure that cache is ephemeral and scrubbed on session end, but i'll include the cache retention doc.
[05:39] Rina: please include specifics on how long cache entries live and what scrub processes run.
[05:44] Samir: will do.
[05:46] Carlos: small nit: earlier in the onboarding we had an error 'invalid endpoint token' when trying to call the API from our CI. any suggestions?
[05:53] Priya: that usually means the token is scoped to a different project. check the project id in the header, and ensure token has the env permission. we'll run the CI token with you after the call if needed.
[06:06] Jordan: let's go rapid-fire through outstanding compliance docs you need. Maya?
[06:10] Maya: SOC 2 Type II report, security questionnaire (SIG-lite), penetration test summary, encryption details, SAML attribute list, audit log schema, retention/export steps, data processing agreement.
[06:22] Jordan: checklist captured. Samir will deliver SOC2 and mapping; Priya will deliver SAML guide; I'll share pricing note on extended retention for Dedicated if you choose later.
[06:35] Rina: timeline note: our auditors need materials by 2025-08-28 for an internal review.
[06:41] Jordan: ack, we'll prioritize.
[06:44] Priya: one more technical note - telemetry sampling for traces. by default we sample 1% of request/response payloads for quality monitoring; for the pilot we can set that to 0% which disables payload capture.
[06:58] Carlos: please set to 0% in staging.
[07:01] Priya: done, will configure after the meeting.
[07:05] Jordan: ok next steps recap: Jordan send SOC 2 and security whitepaper, Priya send SAML config and export examples, Samir send audit log schema and cache retention docs, Sentinel to confirm SAML attributes and provide test user, and staging will be configured for 90-day audit window and 0% payload sampling.
[07:25] Maya: that sounds good. can we get a short Slack thread or email with the links to the docs after?
[07:30] Jordan: yes will email the links and attach files.
[07:32] Dr. Cho: quick question on service-levels for Dedicated later - any rough latency/throughput numbers?
[07:38] Jordan: high level, Dedicated is designed for predictable throughput, our perf docs have p95 latency numbers per model, i'll share the benchmark sheet.
[07:46] Carlos: ok we'll review.
[07:49] Rina: last item - privacy wants the legal contact for contracting.
[07:52] Jordan: legal is emily park, cc me and i'll intro.
[07:55] Maya: thanks everyone.
[07:57] Jordan: thanks all, meeting adjourned.
---
End of transcript.
